content:
The experimental Raman spectrum shows a strong C-H stretching region (2879–2972 cm⁻¹), a carbonyl stretch (1727 cm⁻¹), and a CH₂ bending mode (1454 cm⁻¹). These features are characteristic of aliphatic carbonyl compounds.

Candidate 4, `CC(C)(C)CC(=O)C=O` (3,3-dimethyl-4-oxobutanal), contains a tert-butyl group, a methylene group, a ketone, and an aldehyde. The presence of the tert-butyl group is consistent with the intense C-H stretching modes observed at 2913, 2938, and 2972 cm⁻¹. The peak at 1727 cm⁻¹ is a classic signature of a carbonyl (C=O) stretching vibration. The peak at 1454 cm⁻¹ corresponds to the CH₂/CH₃ bending modes. The lower frequency peaks (598, 767, 800 cm⁻¹) are consistent with skeletal vibrations of branched aliphatic chains. Other candidates, such as those containing ethers or cyclic structures, do not match the specific intensity distribution of the C-H stretching region as well as this branched aliphatic aldehyde/ketone.

SELECTED_INDEX: 4
CONFIDENCE: 0.85
EXPLANATION: The spectrum is dominated by aliphatic C-H stretching (2879-2972 cm⁻¹) and a clear carbonyl stretch at 1727 cm⁻¹, which is highly characteristic of the 3,3-dimethyl-4-oxobutanal structure. The CH₂ bending at 1454 cm⁻¹ further supports this assignment.
